title: Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 1.III: grace that only warns and persuades, leaving the will under free will’s dice, is law not proper grace — Aug. De grat. Christi 13–14
pass_a_gloss: But concerning that grace which only warns and persuades, but leaves the Will itself as it were under the uncertain dice of its free will, Augustine judges that it looks rather unto law than unto grace properly so called: He who knows what ought to be done, and does not, has not yet learned from God according to grace, but according to law, De gratia Christi, contra Pelag. cap. 13. And at the beginning of cap. 14. He who has not come is not yet rightly said to have learned: he has indeed heard and learned that one ought to come, but he wills not to do what he has learned. It is by no means rightly said of that mode of teaching by which God teaches through grace.
pass_b_english: But of the grace that only warns and persuades, and leaves the will under free will’s uncertain dice, Augustine holds it looks to law rather than to grace properly so called (De gratia Christi contra Pelagium 13): Who knows what ought to be done and does not, has not yet learned from God according to grace, but according to law. And at the start of 14: Who has not come is not yet rightly said to have learned—he heard and learned that he ought to come, but will not do what he learned. That mode of teaching is not rightly called the way God teaches by grace.
source_text: De illa autem gratia quae monet et suadet tantum, sed ipsam Voluntatem quasi sub alea incerta liberi sui arbitrii relinquit, sentit Augustinus, ad legem potius eam spectare quam ad gratiam proprie dictam: Qui novit quid fieri debeat, et non facit, nondum a Deo didicit secundum gratiam, sed secundum legem, De gratia Christi, contra Pelag. cap. 13. Et initio cap. 14. Qui non venit, nondum ille recte dicitur didicisse: audivit quidem et didicit oportere veniendum, sed facere non vult quod didicit. Prorsus non recte dicitur de isto docendi modo, quo per gratiam docet Deus.
